chapter.li: LEChapter17 Verse1 When Abinadi had finished speaking, the king ordered the priests to take him and have him put to death. VerseEnd Verse2 But there was one among them named Alma, a young man and a descendant of Nephi, who believed Abinadi’s words, since he could see the iniquity Abinadi had testified against them. Therefore he started to plead with the king not to be angry with Abinadi, but to let him leave in peace. VerseEnd Verse3 But the king became even angrier and had Alma thrown out and sent servants to kill him. VerseEnd Verse4 But he escaped and hid and they didn’t find him. While in hiding for many days, Alma wrote down everything Abinadi had said. VerseEnd

Verse5 The king had his guards surround Abinadi and take him, tie him up, and throw him in prison. VerseEnd Verse6 The king consulted with his priests and after three days, he had Abinadi brought back. VerseEnd Verse7 Then he announced: Abinadi, we’ve found 2PSI you guilty, and 2PSI you deserve to be executed. VerseEnd Verse8 2PSI You claim that God Himself would come down among mankind. And now for saying this, 2PSI you’ll be put to death unless 2PSI you retract everything 2PSI you’ve falsely testified about me and my people. VerseEnd

Verse9 And Abinadi said to him: I won’t retract anything I’ve said to 2PSF you, because it’s all true. To prove I’m testifying of the truth, I’ve let 2PSF you capture me. VerseEnd Verse10 And I will let 2PSF you execute me, but I won’t retract my words, and they’ll stand as a testimony condemning 2PSF you. If 2PSF you kill me, 2PSF you will shed innocent blood, which will also condemn 2PSF you on the last day. VerseEnd

Verse11 Now king Noah was about to release him, because he was afraid of what he had been told, and worried God’s judgments would fall on him. VerseEnd Verse12 But the priests cried out loudly in opposition, accusing and claiming: He’s insulted the king! So the king was provoked to anger against him, and he instead decided to have him executed. VerseEnd

Verse13 They then took him, tied him up, set him atop firewood, and burned him to death. VerseEnd Verse14 And when the flames began to burn him, he yelled to them, saying: VerseEnd Verse15 Just as 2PP you’ve done to me, 2PP your descendants will also do to many others who will suffer the same pain that I suffer — painful death by fire — because they believe in the salvation of the Lord who is God. VerseEnd Verse16 2PP You’ll be infected by many diseases because of 2PP your iniquities. VerseEnd Verse17 2PP You’ll be attacked on all sides and driven and scattered, just like a wild flock driven by hungry predators. VerseEnd Verse18 At that time 2PP you’ll be hunted and taken by 2PP your enemies. Then 2PP you will, like me, feel the pain of being executed by burning. VerseEnd Verse19 This is how God repays those who destroy His people. O God, receive my spirit! VerseEnd Verse20 Now when Abinadi had said this, he collapsed, dying in the fire, having been executed because he wouldn’t deny God’s commandments, having sealed the truth of his words through his death. VerseEnd

LEChapter18 Verse1 Now Alma, who escaped from king Noah’s servants, repented of his sins and iniquities and began secretly teaching Abinadi’s words to others: VerseEnd Verse2 about what was coming, the resurrection of the dead, and the redemption of mankind, which was accomplished through Christ’s power, suffering, death, resurrection, and ascension into heaven. VerseEnd Verse3 He taught all those who would listen to him, teaching them privately so it wouldn’t become known to the king. And many believed what he taught. VerseEnd Verse4 Those who believed him went to a place called Mormon, which was in the frontier of the land. It had received its name from the king and was sometimes overrun by wild animals. VerseEnd Verse5 There was a spring of pure water in Mormon, and Alma hid there during the day in a thicket of small trees near the water, to avoid the king’s pursuit. VerseEnd Verse6 And all those who believed him went there to hear him teach. VerseEnd Verse7 After many days, a large group who believed gathered at Mormon to hear Alma’s teaching. He instructed them about repentance, redemption, and faith in the Lord. VerseEnd

Verse8 He told them: Here are the waters of Mormon (referring to what they were called). Do 2PP you have a desire to enter God’s fold and be called His people? Are 2PP you willing to help carry each other’s burdens, to lighten them for one another? VerseEnd Verse9 Are 2PP you willing to mourn with those who mourn, and comfort those who need comforting? Will 2PP you stand and testify as witnesses of God at all times, in all things, wherever 2PP you go, for the rest of 2PP your lives? Do 2PP you want to qualify for redemption by God and be included with those of the first resurrection, receiving eternal life? VerseEnd Verse10 If this is the desire of 2PP your hearts, are 2PP you now willing to be baptized in the Lord’s name, as a witness before Him that 2PP you’ve made a covenant with Him? Are 2PP you willing to commit to serve Him and keep His commandments, so He can pour out His Spirit more abundantly upon 2PP you? VerseEnd Verse11 Now when the people heard this, they applauded and shouted: This is our heart’s desire! VerseEnd

Verse12 Then Alma took Helam — one of the first — and went and stood in the water and prayed: O Lord, pour out 2PSI Your Spirit upon 2PSI Your servant, so he can do this work with holiness of heart. VerseEnd Verse13 And when he had prayed these words, the Spirit of the Lord filled him and he said: Helam, I baptize 2PSF you, having authority from Almighty God, as a demonstration that 2PSF you’ve made a covenant to serve Him for the remainder of 2PSF your mortal life. And may the Spirit of the Lord be poured out upon 2PSF you, and may He grant 2PSF you eternal life through Christ’s redemption, which He prepared from the beginning of creation. VerseEnd Verse14 After Alma said these words, both Alma and Helam submerged in the water. And they resurfaced rejoicing, filled with the Spirit. VerseEnd Verse15 Then Alma took another and went into the water again and baptized him in the same way as the first, only he didn’t submerge himself again. VerseEnd Verse16 He baptized every one in this way — about 204 people — who gathered at the place of Mormon. And they were baptized in the waters of Mormon and were filled with God’s grace. VerseEnd Verse17 They were called the congregation of God, or the congregation of Christ, from that time forward. And whoever was baptized by God’s power and authority was added to His congregation. VerseEnd

Verse18 And Alma, having authority from God, ordained priests, one priest for every 50. He ordained them to preach and teach concerning God’s kingdom. VerseEnd Verse19 And he commanded them to only teach the things he and the holy prophets had taught. VerseEnd Verse20 To be clear, he commanded them to preach nothing but repentance and faith in the Lord, who had redeemed His people. VerseEnd Verse21 And he commanded them not to have any heated arguments with each other, but to look forward with one eye, having one faith and one baptism, having their hearts bound together in unity and love toward each other. VerseEnd Verse22 This is how he commanded them to preach. And so they became God’s children. VerseEnd

Verse23 He also commanded them to keep the Sabbath holy, and to give thanks to the Lord God every day. VerseEnd Verse24 He also commanded them that the priests he ordained were to work with their own hands for their support. VerseEnd Verse25 And there was one day in every week set apart for them to gather, to teach the people and to worship the Lord their God. They met as often as they could. VerseEnd Verse26 And the priests didn’t depend on the people to pay them, but they were to receive God’s grace as payment, so they could grow in faith, receiving inspiration from God, enabling them to teach with power and authority from God. VerseEnd

Verse27 Alma also commanded the congregation members to give freely of their material possessions, each one based upon what they had. If they had a lot, they were to give a lot. But only a little would be expected of those who only had a little. And those who had nothing were to receive. VerseEnd Verse28 So they were to give their donations voluntarily, out of their love for God, including to priests in need, and also to every needy, helpless soul. VerseEnd Verse29 He told them this was a commandment from God. And they obeyed God, giving to each other both temporally and spiritually according to their needs and circumstances. VerseEnd

Verse30 Now this was accomplished in the place called Mormon, by the waters of Mormon, in the forest that was near the waters of Mormon. The place of Mormon, the waters of Mormon, the forest of Mormon — how sacred a place for those who came to know their Redeemer there! How blessed they are! They’ll sing praises to Him forever! VerseEnd

Verse31 These things were done in the outskirts of the land to escape the notice of the king. VerseEnd Verse32 But the king, noticing the conduct of the people, sent his servants to follow them. So on the day they assembled to hear the Lord’s word, they were betrayed and revealed to the king. VerseEnd Verse33 Now the king accused Alma of inciting the people to rebellion against him. So he sent his army to kill them. VerseEnd Verse34 But Alma and the Lord’s people learned the king’s army was coming. Therefore they took their tents and families and fled into the wilderness, VerseEnd Verse35 about 450 people in number. VerseEnd

LEChapter19 Verse1 And the king’s army was unable to locate them and therefore returned. VerseEnd Verse2 Now the king’s soldiers were reduced to only a few. A disagreement arose involving the rest of the people. VerseEnd Verse3 The minority started making threats against the king and a great struggle began. VerseEnd Verse4 Then a man named Gideon — a strong man who was an enemy of the king — drew his sword and swore in anger he would kill the king. VerseEnd Verse5 And he fought with the king. When the king saw Gideon was going to overpower him, he fled, running up the tower near the temple. VerseEnd Verse6 But Gideon chased him and was getting ready to climb the tower to kill the king when the king noticed a Lamanite army was invading from the land of Shemlon. VerseEnd Verse7 Now the king pleaded pitifully: Gideon, spare me! The Lamanites are about to attack us and they’ll kill my people. VerseEnd Verse8 Now the king wasn’t really concerned about his people but valued his own life. Nevertheless, Gideon spared his life. VerseEnd

Verse9 And the king ordered the people to flee from the Lamanites, and he ran in front of them. They fled into the wilderness with their women and children. VerseEnd Verse10 But the Lamanites pursued and caught up with them, and began killing them. VerseEnd Verse11 So the king ordered the men to abandon their wives and children and run from the Lamanites. VerseEnd Verse12 However, there were many who refused to leave them, preferring to stay and die with them. But the rest abandoned their wives and children and ran away. VerseEnd

Verse13 Those who stayed with their wives and children had their beautiful daughters go out and beg the Lamanites not to kill them. VerseEnd Verse14 And because they were attracted by the beauty of their women, the Lamanites took pity on them. VerseEnd Verse15 So the Lamanites spared their lives, taking them prisoner. They took them back to the land of Nephi, allowing them to live there under the condition that they would hand over king Noah to the Lamanites and pay them half of everything they owned — half their gold, silver, and valuables. They would have to pay this tribute to the king of the Lamanites yearly. VerseEnd Verse16 One of king Noah’s sons, named Limhi, was among the prisoners. VerseEnd Verse17 Although Limhi didn’t want his father to be killed, he was aware of his father’s iniquities. Limhi was a righteous man. VerseEnd

Verse18 Gideon secretly sent men into the wilderness to search for the king and those with him. They located the missing people, all except for the king and his priests. VerseEnd Verse19 Now these people had vowed they would return to the land of Nephi; and if their wives, children, and those who remained with them had been killed, then they would take revenge and die with them. VerseEnd Verse20 But the king ordered them not to return, and they became so angry with the king they executed him by burning him to death. VerseEnd Verse21 They were about to execute the priests too, but they escaped. VerseEnd

Verse22 They were returning to the land of Nephi when they met Gideon’s soldiers, who told them everything that had happened to their wives and children. They learned the Lamanites allowed them to live on the land as long as they paid them a tax of half of all they owned. VerseEnd Verse23 They informed Gideon’s soldiers that they had killed the king and that his priests ran into the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse24 After they finished the discussion, they returned to the land of Nephi, rejoicing because their wives and children hadn’t been killed; and they told Gideon they executed the king. VerseEnd

Verse25 Following this the king of the Lamanites committed to them that his people wouldn’t kill them. VerseEnd Verse26 And Limhi, the king’s son, by a vote of the people, had the kingdom conferred on him. He also agreed with the king of the Lamanites that his people would pay taxes to him of half of everything they had. VerseEnd

Verse27 So Limhi began to administer the kingdom and there was peace among his people. VerseEnd Verse28 The king of the Lamanites put guards surrounding the land to confine Limhi’s people, so they couldn’t escape into the wilderness. He supported his guards from the taxes paid by the Nephites. VerseEnd Verse29 Now king Limhi had two years of peace in his kingdom, and the Lamanites didn’t harass them or try to kill them during that time. VerseEnd

LEChapter20 Verse1 There was a place in Shemlon where the Lamanite young women went to sing, dance, and entertain themselves. VerseEnd Verse2 One day a small number of them gathered to sing and dance. VerseEnd Verse3 Because king Noah’s priests were ashamed to return to the city of Nephi, and fearing the people would kill them, they didn’t dare return to their wives and children. VerseEnd Verse4 They hid in the wilderness and discovered the Lamanite young women, watching them and waiting in ambush. VerseEnd Verse5 When there were only a few of them gathered to dance, they emerged from their hiding place, took 24 of them, and forced them into the wilderness. VerseEnd

Verse6 When the Lamanites found out their daughters were missing, they blamed Limhi’s people, concluding that they were the ones who had kidnapped them. VerseEnd Verse7 So they sent their armies out — led by the king himself — and they went up to the land of Nephi to attack and kill Limhi’s people. VerseEnd Verse8 Now Limhi saw them from the tower preparing to attack. So he gathered his people and waited in ambush for them in the fields and forests. VerseEnd Verse9 Then, when the Lamanites arrived, Limhi’s people began to ambush and kill them. VerseEnd

Verse10 The battle became very severe, because they fought like lions for their prey. VerseEnd Verse11 And despite not being half as many as the Lamanites, Limhi’s people began to prevail over the Lamanites, since they were fighting for their lives, wives, and children. Therefore they drove themselves onward, fighting like wild predators. VerseEnd

Verse12 After the battle was over, they found the king of the Lamanites alive among the bodies of the fallen Lamanites. His people abandoned the fight so quickly that he had been forgotten, wounded on the ground. VerseEnd Verse13 So they took him, bandaged his wounds, and brought him to Limhi, saying: Here is the king of the Lamanites. He was wounded and fell among their dead, and they left him. We’ve brought him here to 2PSF you. Let’s kill him! VerseEnd Verse14 But Limhi told them: Don’t kill him, bring him here to see me. So they brought him, and Limhi asked: Why have 2PSF you come up to fight my people? My people haven’t broken the agreement I had with 2PSF you. So why have 2PSF you broken the agreement 2PSF you swore to my people? VerseEnd Verse15 The king replied: I’ve broken the agreement because 2PSI your people kidnapped some of my people’s daughters. I was furious because of that, and so I had my people attack 2PSI your people. VerseEnd Verse16 Now Limhi had heard nothing about this. So he said: I’ll search for them among my people, and whoever has done this will die. Therefore he searched for them among his people. VerseEnd

Verse17 Now when Gideon, the king’s captain, heard about this, he came and said to the king: Please don’t bother investigating our people; don’t accuse them of this. VerseEnd Verse18 Don’t 2PP you remember 2PSI your father’s priests we tried to kill? Aren’t they hiding in the wilderness? Isn’t it apparent they’ve kidnapped the Lamanite young women? VerseEnd Verse19 Think about it and go tell the king about them, so that he can explain it to his people and they can be reassured about us. They’re already getting ready to attack again and we have only a few able to fight. VerseEnd Verse20 Their large army outnumbers us and we will be killed unless their king explains we are innocent. VerseEnd Verse21 It’s clear that Abinadi’s prophesy against us is happening — all because we refused to listen to the Lord’s word and turn from our iniquities. VerseEnd Verse22 So let’s satisfy the king and fulfill the agreement we have made with him. Slavery is better than death. Therefore let’s put a stop to all this killing. VerseEnd Verse23 Then Limhi told the king all about his father and the priests who had fled into the wilderness, attributing their daughters’ kidnapping to them. VerseEnd

Verse24 So the king of the Lamanites was satisfied with Limhi’s people, and he said to them: Let’s go out unarmed to meet my people; and I give 2PP you my solemn oath that my people won’t kill 2PSI your people. VerseEnd Verse25 They followed the king, going out unarmed to meet the Lamanites. When they met the Lamanites, the king of the Lamanites bowed before them and pled on behalf of Limhi’s people. VerseEnd Verse26 When the Lamanites saw Limhi’s people were unarmed, they felt sympathy for them and were satisfied, and returned peacefully with their king to their own land. VerseEnd

LEChapter21 Verse1 Then Limhi and his people returned to the city of Nephi, living again in peace. VerseEnd Verse2 As time passed, however, the Lamanites once more became angry with the Nephites, and they began to cross the borders of the surrounding land. VerseEnd Verse3 Now they didn’t dare kill them because of their king’s commitment to Limhi, but they would hit them in the face, exercise authority over them, lay heavy loads on their backs, and drive them like pack mules. VerseEnd Verse4 This was all done to fulfill the Lord’s word. VerseEnd Verse5 The Nephites were tormented. But there was no way for them to free themselves, since the Lamanites surrounded them on all sides. VerseEnd

Verse6 The people began to complain to the king because of their afflictions, wishing to retaliate. They greatly troubled the king with their complaints, so that he let them do as they wanted. VerseEnd Verse7 They gathered again, put on their armor, and went out against the Lamanites to push them off their land. VerseEnd Verse8 But the Lamanites beat them, drove them back, and killed many of them. VerseEnd Verse9 That resulted in great mourning and lamentation among Limhi’s people, the widow mourning her husband, the son and daughter mourning their father, and brothers mourning brothers. VerseEnd

Verse10 Now there were many widows in the land, and they complained continually every day, because a great fear of the Lamanites terrorized them. VerseEnd Verse11 Their continual complaining stirred up the rest of Limhi’s people to be angry at the Lamanites, so they went once more to battle. But they were defeated again, and many were killed. VerseEnd Verse12 But they tried again a third time and suffered similarly, and those who survived returned to the city of Nephi. VerseEnd Verse13 Then they humbled themselves to the dust, submitting themselves to the burdens of slavery, letting themselves be beaten, herded here and there, and treated like pack mules, according to their enemies’ whims. VerseEnd Verse14 They humbled themselves in the depths of humility, praying humbly to God — indeed, they prayed to God all day long, asking Him to end their suffering. VerseEnd

Verse15 Now the Lord was slow to answer their prayers because of their iniquities. Nevertheless, the Lord answered their prayers and began to soften the Lamanites’ hearts, and they began to ease their burdens. But the Lord didn’t see fit to free them from slavery. VerseEnd

Verse16 Gradually they began to make progress in the land raising grain, flocks, and herds more successfully, so they didn’t suffer hunger. VerseEnd Verse17 Now there were many more women than men. Therefore king Limhi ordered the men to help support the widows and their children, to prevent starvation. This was because so many had been killed. VerseEnd Verse18 Now Limhi’s people stayed close together when possible to protect their grain and flocks. VerseEnd Verse19 And the king himself didn’t feel safe outside the city walls unless he had his guards with him. He feared being captured by the Lamanites. VerseEnd Verse20 He had his people watch the surrounding land, hoping to capture those priests who had fled into the wilderness and kidnapped the Lamanite young women, causing them such great destruction. VerseEnd Verse21 They wanted to capture them to punish them. They came into the land of Nephi at night and stole their grain and valuable property. Therefore they set an ambush for them. VerseEnd

Verse22 There had been no more unrest between the Lamanites and Limhi’s people, up to the time that Ammon and his men came into the land. VerseEnd Verse23 And the king, while outside the city gates with his guard, encountered Ammon and his men. Thinking them to be Noah’s priests, he had them arrested, tied up, and thrown in prison. Had they been Noah’s priests, he would have had them executed. VerseEnd Verse24 But when he found they were not, and they were fellow Nephites who had come from Zarahemla, he was delighted. VerseEnd

Verse25 Now king Limhi, before Ammon’s coming, had sent a small number of men to search for the land of Zarahemla, but they couldn’t find it. They got lost in the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse26 Despite that, they found a place that had been inhabited and was now covered with dry bones. It obviously had been occupied by people who were destroyed. They assumed it was Zarahemla, so they returned to the land of Nephi, arriving at the outskirts of the land only a few days before Ammon’s arrival. VerseEnd Verse27 And they carried with them a record engraved on metal plates of the people whose bones they had found. VerseEnd Verse28 Now Limhi was again very pleased upon learning from Ammon that king Benjamin had a gift from God that let him interpret such engravings. Ammon was also pleased. VerseEnd Verse29 But Ammon and his men grieved because so many of Limhi’s people had been killed VerseEnd Verse30 and that king Noah and his priests had led the people to commit so many sins and iniquities against God. They also mourned Abinadi’s death and the departure of Alma and the people who went with him, who had formed a congregation of God through God’s strength and power and through faith in the words spoken by Abinadi. VerseEnd Verse31 Indeed, they missed them because they didn’t know where they could be found. If they knew how to locate them, they would have gladly joined them, since they too had made a covenant with God to serve Him and keep His commandments. VerseEnd Verse32 Since Ammon’s arrival, king Limhi and many of his people had also made a covenant with God to serve Him and keep His commandments. VerseEnd

Verse33 And king Limhi and many of his people wanted to be baptized, but there was no one available who had authority from God. Ammon declined to do it because he considered himself an unworthy servant. VerseEnd Verse34 Therefore they didn’t form themselves into a congregation at that time, waiting on the Spirit of the Lord. Now they wanted to become just like Alma and his people who had fled into the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse35 They wanted to be baptized as a witness and testimony they were willing to serve God with all their hearts. Nevertheless, they waited, and an account of their baptism will be included later. VerseEnd Verse36 Now the entire focus and planning of Ammon, king Limhi, and his people was to escape from the Lamanites and get free from slavery. VerseEnd
